blocks.content: The Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and protected by the Constitution, making the Supreme Court the defender and guarantor of these rights.

rows: Justiciable and directly enforceable by courts
Can be suspended during National Emergency (except Arts 20 & 21)
Permanent constitutional guidelines, no suspension required

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights are justiciable in nature, allowing citizens to move the courts directly for their enforcement.
These rights are not absolute but qualified, meaning the State can impose reasonable restrictions on them.
Parliament can curtail or repeal any Fundamental Right by a Constitutional Amendment Act under Article 368 without altering the basic structure.
Rights guaranteed under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
Fundamental Rights under Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available exclusively to Indian citizens.
Articles 20 and 21 remain enforceable even during a National Emergency declared under Article 352.
Article 19 rights are automatically suspended ONLY when National Emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.
Fundamental Rights under Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are conferred on citizens alone, whereas other rights extend to both citizens and foreigners.
